newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan Kubo says yen movements reflect fundamentals.
newsitem.headline: Japan Kubo says yen movements reflect fundamentals.

text.p: Finance Minister Wataru Kubo said on Tuesday that the yen's current movements in the foreign exchange market basically reflect economic fundamentals.
He told a news conference that he did not think the yen's current movements were a big problem, adding: "I don't think the situation warrants special attention to the issue."
He added that the dollar was still in the process of orderly reversal.

"Current foreign exchange movements are part of a big trend which emerged when G7 leaders agreed last April to work to correct this (the dollar's weakness) through close cooperation and coordination between them in the currency market," Kubo said.
Japan may need to seriously consider measures to take regarding the foreign exchange market if currency fluctuations become too sudden or fail to reflect economic fundamentals, he said.
Regarding a supplementary budget for this fiscal year, Kubo said: "There is no need to formulate a large supplementary budget which includes investment in public works."
He said Japanese businesses have not strongly asked for such a stimulative package, and that the government must also consider the big deficit in state finances.

Drawing up an extra budget would take about a month and a half, and the government must also consider the effect this would have on the schedule for drafting the full-year budget for 1997/98, he said.
